title: Worksheet 15: Choosing the Right Data Structure
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Programmers regularly must decide which data structure best fits the specific problem they are trying to solve, since choosing the wrong one can make a program slower, harder to understand, or more difficult to maintain over time. A single variable is often best for storing one individual piece of information, such as a player's current score. A list is generally a strong choice when a program needs to store multiple related items in a specific order, especially when that collection of items might need to grow, shrink, or be looped through later. A dictionary tends to work well when information needs to be organized using clear, descriptive labels rather than simple numeric positions, such as storing a person's different pieces of contact information. A tuple is often chosen specifically when a collection of values should remain fixed and unchanged throughout the entire program. There is rarely only one "correct" answer when choosing a data structure, but understanding the strengths of each option helps a programmer make a more thoughtful and deliberate decision.
